finding: The MCP smoke observes the browser request sequence and retained screenshot artifact independently, but a deliberately adversarial writable profile can still replay requests or forge a PNG. Deterministic WorkflowPlatform checks and owner acceptance remain separate authorities.

reported.title: Zodchi b868767b-78db-4115-88fc-1090b81213a3
reported.evidence: Playwright MCP only (no shell/HTTP/subprocess/other agent). Steps: browser_resize -> viewport 1280x800 (>= 800x600, confirmed in-page: window.innerWidth=1280, window.innerHeight=800); browser_navigate -> http://127.0.0.1:58087/zodchi-browser-b96dea78-4a26-4b50-9dd5-121bd19a750f (final location.href identical, document.readyState="complete", so the page script had run); browser_evaluate read document.title = "Zodchi b868767b-78db-4115-88fc-1090b81213a3" and document.body.innerText = "Body fa60a526-2f5d-451c-af95-37f7fb907258"; browser_snapshot showed a single main landmark with the same text. Note the title/body UUIDs are script-generated and differ from the URL UUID. browser_take_screenshot (type=png, scale=css, viewport) was called with filename "<project>\docs\evidence\claude-playwright-mcp-windows-0.6.12.png" and returned successfully; the server echoed the saved artifact as "docs\evidence\claude-playwright-mcp-windows-0.6.12.png" (displayed relative to <project>, unlike its own output-dir artifacts which echo with a ".playwright-mcp\" prefix), which indicates the absolute target path was honored. I could not independently confirm the bytes on disk: file: protocol navigation is blocked by the MCP server and this profile has no filesystem/shell tools, so the on-disk path is asserted from the server's own success response, not verified by a second read. Navigation also reported 1 console error; its contents were not inspected as it was outside the task scope.
